source: en.wikipedia.org, "Margaret Fulton" (page 10991710): By 1978 it had sold "more than two-thirds of a million copies". Wiktionary, "third", noun: "One of three equal parts of a whole."; two thirds of a million is 2 x 1000000 / 3 = 2000000/3, which is no whole number, so the kind is fraction.

text: At that point 3 quarters of the votes were counted.
source: Collins, "quarter", sense 2: "Also called: fourth the fraction equal to one divided by four (1/4)"; arithmetic: 3/4 = 0.75; "point" with no number before it is a noun, not a decimal marker

text: The gap was 2.5 hundredths.
source: Wiktionary, "hundredth": "one of a hundred equal parts of a whole"; arithmetic: 2.5 x 1/100 = 0.025
